info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary: listCampaigns returns the caller org's ad campaigns, optionally filtered by status.
get.description: listCampaigns returns the caller org's ad campaigns, optionally filtered by status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status narrows the list to one lifecycle state: draft, active, paused or completed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: createCampaign registers an ad campaign in the caller's org.
post.description:
createCampaign registers an ad campaign in the caller's org. Name is required;
platform defaults to meta and status to draft, budget and spend are minor units
clamped to >= 0, and the id, createdAt, updatedAt and externalId of the input are
ignored — the server assigns them. Nothing is spent: a campaign is a plan until it
is launched.

delete.summary: deleteCampaign removes one of the caller org's ad campaigns and answers 204.
delete.description:
deleteCampaign removes one of the caller org's ad campaigns and answers 204. It
deletes the stored plan only — a campaign already running at the provider is not
stopped there.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: getCampaign returns one of the caller org's ad campaigns.
get.description: getCampaign returns one of the caller org's ad campaigns.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

put.summary: updateCampaign replaces one of the caller org's ad campaigns.
put.description:
updateCampaign replaces one of the caller org's ad campaigns. It is a full replace,
not a patch: name is required and every omitted field resets to its default. The
campaign updated is the one the PATH names — a body id cannot retarget it — and
createdAt and externalId are server-owned.

post.summary: launchCampaign runs a stored campaign on its provider and starts spending.
post.description:
launchCampaign runs a stored campaign on its provider and starts spending. It holds
no token: the org's connected ad-account credential is resolved from KMS at call
time and the launch FAILS CLOSED with 424 when the org has not connected that
platform, so it can never spend on a connection the org did not make. On success the
provider campaign id is recorded and the campaign goes active.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

get.summary: summary returns the caller org's campaign counts and money totals.
get.description: summary returns the caller org's campaign counts and money totals.

active.description: Active is how many of them are in the active state.

budget.description: Budget is the total budget across campaigns, in minor units.

campaigns.description: Campaigns is how many campaigns the org has.

spend.description: Spend is the total recorded spend across campaigns, in minor units.

externalId.description: provider campaign id after a launch

data.description: Data is the matching campaigns, newest first.

account.description:
Account sets or overrides the provider ad account to spend from; empty uses the
account already stored on the campaign.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.
